DIY Accounting Submit

Do you need Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, and when do you start?

Give your income for three tax years and see your start date, your first update deadline and the records to keep

Making Tax Digital for Income Tax starts on 6 April 2026, 6 April 2027 or 6 April 2028, by how much self-employment and property income you had. Give your income for each tax year below. The page shows your start date, your first quarterly update deadline and the records to keep. Submit's Income Tax filing awaits HMRC recognition. VAT returns are filed today: see VAT return from a spreadsheet.

See the Making Tax Digital dates

Check your income

Type your income before expenses for each tax year. Leave a box empty for no income. The answer is the earliest start date that your income gives.

What counts as qualifying income

The thresholds below apply to your qualifying income. Add your self-employment income and your property income, each before expenses.

This is the amount before expenses (also known as turnover), based on the tax return you submitted in the previous tax year.

gov.uk/guidance/work-out-your-qualifying-income-for-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 13 November 2026

Who the rule covers

The rule covers sole traders and landlords who are registered for Self Assessment.

you’re a sole trader or a landlord registered for Self Assessment

gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 13 November 2026

The three start dates

Each start date has its own threshold and tax year.

£50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year, you should’ve started using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026

gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 13 November 2026

£30,000 for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2027

gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 13 November 2026

£20,000 for the 2026 to 2027 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2028

gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 13 November 2026

Your first quarterly update

The first update covers 6 April to 5 July of your start year. It is due on 7 August of that year.

Update period Deadline
6 April to 5 July 7 August
6 April to 5 October 7 November
6 April to 5 January 7 February
6 April to 5 April 7 May, in the following tax year
Source: the table on gov.uk/guidance/use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax/send-quarterly-updates Retrieved 13 November 2026

Records to keep

For each item of income or expense, record the amount, the date when the income was received or expenses incurred, and the category.

You will need to use your software to create digital records.

gov.uk/guidance/use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax/keep-digital-records Retrieved 13 November 2026

What Submit files

The dates for every filing are on the MTD calendar.

Submit's Income Tax (MTD) filing awaits HMRC recognition. Until then it runs against a test service and files nothing real.
